text:
mike.t: heads up — EU-W1 hostpool showing sustained egress credit burn for the last 4m, latency climbing on hosted inference routes :rotating_light:
infra-bot: ALERT eu-west1.egress_credit_burn > 85% for 5m (affected pools: hosted-1, dedicated-eu1). Sampled flows: tenant_42, tenant_88, unknown-burst.
sara: seeing 95th p90 token lat increase in hosted api traces, looks correlated with packets queued at egress-shaper on node-rack-12.
jonathan: any recent deploys to hosted-1?
mike.t: no deploys in the last 30m. metrics show KV cache churn + tcp_retransmits up.
ekaterina: I'm pulling logs now, could be a tenant doing heavy embedding/nearest-neighbor searches. tagging infra-team for noisy-neighbor triage.
sara: quick check: can we soft-quarantine top offenders to dedicated fallback? what does routing look like for hosted->dedicated fallback in eu?
jonathan: fallback path exists but dedicated pool capacity is ~85% used; auto-burst limited. We can trigger a conservative canary: route new requests from affected routes to dedicated-eu2 only if latency > 150ms.
mike.t: agree. also want smoothing on egress credits to avoid cliff. proposal: add transient egress-smoothing token bucket per-tenant (burst window 30s -> amortize over 120s).
ekaterina: sketch of probe command I ran:
```
# show per-tenant egress in last 5m
routectl egress-stats --region eu-west1 --window 5m | grep tenant_
tenant_42  1.2Gb/s  (spike)
tenant_88  800Mb/s
```
sara: tenant_42 is a known embedding customer, might be a bad client-side loop. can we shadow-drop or rate-limit their API key temporarily and notify SE?
jonathan: we can do a soft-rate at the proxy: `proxyctl throttle --key tenant_42 --rate 400mbps --mode soft` — that will return 429 under sustained pressure but keep graceful degradation.
mike.t: please run that, and post back logs. also enable KVcache-prefetch to avoid regen churn on those requests.
ekaterina: applied soft throttle at 1847654350. seeing egress drop for tenant_42 from 1.2Gb/s -> 350Mb/s within 20s. p90 latency slowly dropping.
sara: nice. request: add temporary dedicated fallback mapping for tenants with sustained egress>700Mb/s for >2m. ops-cost warning: dedicated fallback will shift cost to reserved capacity.
mike.t: understood. open question: do we want automatic fallback or operator-triggered only? I'm leaning operator-triggered for now to avoid cost surprise.
jonathan: agree. operator-triggered + telemetry alert with clear cost estimate. I'll add a runbook step.
ekaterina: notes for runbook addition: 1) confirm egress pattern 2) soft-throttle key 3) if >2m and latency not improving, trigger `routectl fallback tenant_id -> dedicated-eu2` 4) notify SE + billing.
infra-bot: NOTE added to runbook "egress-noise-fallback-v1" by jonathan at 1847654380.
mike.t: final ask — add short-term smoothing config to proxy and file an infra-ml ticket to look at tenant prediction model (to pre-warm dedicated slices for heavy embedding jobs). Sara can you file?
sara: filing INFRA-7892 with summary + cost estimate now. linking logs. :thumbsup:
jonathan: leaving monitoring on. will follow up in #eng-sre if anything regresses.
mike.t: thanks team — keep this thread for timeline, we'll close once burst is fully drained and runbook verified.
